sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，有线电视运营商也开始提供电话服务。

sentences.en: Now, internet access.
sentences.zh: 现在，轮到互联网接入了。

sentences.en: They don't see themselves as providing a democratic public service function,
sentences.zh: 他们并不认为自己是在履行民主的公共服务职能，

sentences.en: and they have really held on to the right to just charge whatever they want
sentences.zh: 他们一直坚持有权随意收取费用，

sentences.en: for access to that wire and raise prices whenever they feel like it.
sentences.zh: 并随时随地提高接入线路的价格。

sentences.en: The cable companies argue that net neutrality regulations would be burdensome and unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 有线电视公司辩称，网络中立性法规既繁琐又没必要。

sentences.en: Market competition, they say, protects the American consumer.
sentences.zh: 他们声称，市场竞争能够保护美国消费者。

sentences.en: But Susan Crawford, who was part of Obama's 2009 FCC transition team,
sentences.zh: 但曾参与奥巴马2009年联邦通信委员会过渡团队的苏珊·克劳福德表示，

sentences.en: says competition disappeared a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 竞争早已不复存在。

sentences.en: We used to think that competition between the telephone companies and the cable guys
sentences.zh: 我们曾以为电话公司和有线电视公司之间的竞争

sentences.en: would protect Americans, and on that basis back in 2002, we deregulated the entire sector.
sentences.zh: 会保护美国人，基于此，我们在2002年对整个行业进行了去监管化。

sentences.en: You know, no more federal oversight.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，不再有联邦监管了。

sentences.en: Go ahead, charge whatever you want, because competition will be the cop on the beat.
sentences.zh: 尽管去收钱吧，因为竞争会成为那个守门人。

sentences.en: If you remember back over a decade ago, there used to be tons of internet service providers,
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得十多年前，那时有大量的互联网服务提供商，

sentences.en: and it never really occurred to me why all those options went away
sentences.zh: 我一直没想明白为什么那些选择都消失了，

sentences.en: and a cable company became the only option for a lot of people when it comes to high-speed internet.
sentences.zh: 而有线电视公司成了许多人高速上网的唯一选择。

sentences.en: And it all boils down to something fundamental in the internet infrastructure, the wires.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这与互联网基础设施的一个基本要素有关，那就是电缆。

sentences.en: The telephone companies had old copper wiring that couldn't handle internet network traffic,
sentences.zh: 电话公司拥有无法处理互联网网络流量的旧铜线，

sentences.en: and they just kind of gave up.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上就放弃了。

sentences.en: The telephone companies realized it was just too expensive
sentences.zh: 电话公司意识到，挖掘旧铜线并用光纤替换它们

sentences.en: to dig up their old copper wires and replace them with fiber.
sentences.zh: 成本实在太高了。

sentences.en: By contrast, all the cable companies have to do to upgrade the service they offer,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，有线电视公司升级服务所要做的，

sentences.en: is to update the electronics.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是更新电子设备。

sentences.en: Don't have to dig up the wire, just put new gear on the back of your wires.
sentences.zh: 不需要挖掘电缆，只需在现有电缆上安装新设备即可。

sentences.en: Which is really cheap in comparison.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，这非常便宜。

sentences.en: That cost advantage on the cable side has been so great
sentences.zh: 有线电视公司在成本上的优势如此之大，

sentences.en: that the telephone companies have simply dropped out.
sentences.zh: 以至于电话公司干脆退出了竞争。

sentences.en: And the cable companies won by default.
sentences.zh: 而有线电视公司不战而胜。

sentences.en: Leaving us with absolutely no cop in the beat,
sentences.zh: 这让我们彻底失去了监管者，

sentences.en: we've got the worst of both worlds, neither competition nor oversight.
sentences.zh: 我们陷入了最糟糕的境地：既没有竞争，也没有监管。

sentences.en: In the end, it's more like the worst of three worlds,
sentences.zh: 最终，这更像是三种糟糕情况的集合，

sentences.en: it's because when we turn over the future of the internet to a cable company,
sentences.zh: 因为当我们把互联网的未来交给一家有线电视公司时，

sentences.en: Susan Crawford says we don't even get a future.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·克劳福德说，我们甚至连未来都没有了。

sentences.en: What this all amounts to is nothing more than just an entertainment service,
sentences.zh: 这一切最终不过是一种娱乐服务而已，

sentences.en: rather than something that produces new forms of making a living,
sentences.zh: 而不是那种能创造新谋生方式、

sentences.en: new jobs, new ways of inventing valuable things for the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 新工作岗位，以及为世界其他地方发明有价值事物的东西。

sentences.en: We won't have that sandbox to play with.
sentences.zh: 我们将失去那个可以自由探索的沙盒。

sentences.en: Other countries will, but we won't.
sentences.zh: 其他国家会有，但我们不会有。

sentences.en: In America, you may have to get used to being at the back of the line.
sentences.zh: 在美国，你可能得习惯排在队伍的最后。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Benjamin Walker
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由本杰明·沃克制作，

sentences.en: from the radio program Too Much Information from WFMU.
sentences.zh: 他来自WFMU电台的节目《Too Much Information》。

sentences.en: With a little help from me, Roman Mars, and Sam Greenspan.
sentences.zh: 感谢罗曼·马尔斯和萨姆·格林斯潘对我的帮助。

sentences.en: We are a project of KALW 91.7 Local Public Radio in San Francisco
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山KALW 91.7本地公共广播电台

sentences.en: and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 以及旧金山美国建筑师协会的一个项目。

sentences.en: You can find this show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并点赞这个节目。

sentences.en: All of us are on Twitter, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都入驻了Twitter、Instagram和Spotify。

sentences.en: But to find out more about this story, including cool pictures and links,
sentences.zh: 但要了解更多关于这个故事的信息，包括精美的图片和链接，

sentences.en: and listen to all the episodes of 99% Invisible,
sentences.zh: 并收听《99% Invisible》的所有剧集，

sentences.en: you must go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你必须访问99pi.org。
